PullRequest.Title: chat: adopt SDK curated marketplace feeds
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- retrieve curated customization feeds through the Copilot SDK while preserving editorial order and exact catalog identity
- install catalog plugins through the SDK's verified plan/apply flow
- synchronize installed plugin state immediately and after restart using exact repository, path, and version identity
- preserve supplied editorial artwork on Browse cards while retaining fallback icons for failed images

## Screenshot

![Curated customization feeds in Code OSS](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a3d8474-10db-4360-a929-b0871d38a963)

## Validation

- `npm run compile` — passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat --grep "browse card images replace fallback icons and restore them on error|browse cards retain wide catalog images|search result images replace fallback icons and restore them on error"` — 3 passed
- targeted SDK catalog/plugin installation, provider synchronization, and restart/uninstall tests — passed
- targeted ESLint for changed marketplace presentation files — passed
- manual authenticated Code OSS verification — passed

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call order, fixed three-feed Promise.all, per-enabled-source catalog Promise.all, 100-item page bound, and exclusive curated rendering are all explicit in the traced code. Only real-world endpoint duration and enabled-source count vary, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: network/IPC calls and catalog result objects for up to 100 items per enabled source
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each cold or invalidated queryless Browse load now issues the three saved-feed requests plus one catalog request per enabled marketplace source; the catalog service fans those source requests out with Promise.all, so cost grows with enabled sources and returned page sizes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased Browse latency and unnecessary network/IPC traffic
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Queryless Browse performed the ordinary marketplace query once and rendered its results; there were no saved-feed calls whose successful output made that query redundant.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed load starts curated-feed retrieval, immediately awaits the existing full marketplace query, and only afterward consumes the feed result. When any curated section succeeds, renderBrowse uses only curatedSections, so the catalog page fetched here is hidden, yet its slowest enabled source still delays the curated cards.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added branch at lines 1303-1305 starts curated retrieval, while the added/restructured line 1313 still executes the full catalog query in the same load before curated results are consumed; this creates the new duplicate boundary fan-out and makes the old query part of the curated critical path.
Findings.Title: Skip the catalog fallback when curated feeds succeed
Findings.Impact: Opening Browse with the GitHub Feed enabled launches three Agent Host saved-feed RPCs plus the normal fan-out to GitHub Feed, MCP Gallery, connectors, and configured marketplaces. Even if the three curated feeds return quickly, a slow unrelated catalog source blocks the curated UI and all catalog responses are discarded from presentation; source/authentication invalidation repeats the burst.
Findings.Evidence: At lines 1303-1305 loadCatalog starts loadBrowseSections, whose workbench implementation maps the three product feeds through Promise.all and provider.getFeed; line 1313 then awaits marketplaceService.query before awaiting that feed promise at line 1364. CustomizationMarketplaceService.query concurrently invokes every selected source and requests up to the 100-item Browse page size. renderBrowse at lines 1616-1628 renders curated sections exclusively whenever any are nonempty, confirming the catalog results have no consumer in the successful-feed case.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve curated sections first for queryless Browse and run marketplaceService.query only when no nonempty curated section is available (including unsupported/error/empty fallback cases). Preserve the existing cache and cancellation behavior, and keep ordinary queries unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh queryless Customizations Browse with the GitHub Feed enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold/invalidated load, loadCatalog starts curated retrieval, then awaits the ordinary catalog query, then awaits curated retrieval before rendering. Thus both the slowest enabled catalog source and the slowest of the three feeds gate curated cards.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve one saved SDK feed through Agent Host searchCustomizationMarketplace and catalog.getSavedFeed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly three concurrent feed requests per cold or invalidated all-sources/GitHub-Feed Browse load, one for each product-configured feed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No saved-feed boundary calls existed; Browse used only the ordinary catalog query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Promise.all waits for all three, and loadCatalog consumes this result only after the ordinary catalog request completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query every enabled marketplace source for a Browse page of up to 100 items
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent query per enabled effective source; the GitHub Feed source itself crosses Agent Host and invokes SDK catalog search, while MCP Gallery/connectors/configured marketplaces use their existing transports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the sole Browse retrieval and its results were rendered. The diff retains it in the new curated path where successful feeds supersede its output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The source queries are joined by Promise.all, and this whole fan-out is awaited before feed results. When curated sections are nonempty its results are retained in cache but excluded from rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load supplied card artwork through lazy HTML image requests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per rendered card image as it approaches the viewport; failed or overly wide compact images fall back without retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing renderer already loaded catalog icons; the diff additionally projects saved-feed icon URLs and permits wide artwork on Browse cards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Images are lazy and do not gate section data/rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three fixed editorial feeds plus the number of enabled marketplace sources and up to 100 returned catalog items per source; image requests scale with visible curated cards.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three feed calls run concurrently in one Promise.all. Independently, marketplaceService.query runs all enabled source calls concurrently in another Promise.all; both groups overlap, with no shared limiter, for an aggregate burst of three plus the enabled-source count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Completed Browse state is cached by selected source for the page lifetime, so search-to-Browse restoration is warm. Source, configuration, default-account, authentication-session, or recovery changes clear/invalidate it and repeat the cold burst. SDK candidate retention is bounded to 1,000 entries for four minutes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call order, both Promise.all fan-outs, page-size bound, cache invalidations, and exclusive curated rendering were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual endpoint latency, enabled-source count, and feed/card sizes vary, but the duplicate fan-out and critical-path ordering occur deterministically on every cold/invalidated curated load.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: successful curated Browse performs and waits for a full fallback query whose results it does not display.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search customizations, including the newly supported plugin kind
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A nonempty query skips getBrowseSections and awaits the existing merged marketplace query; SDK search returns a bounded page and continuations backfill only when filters require it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query enabled marketplace providers; Agent Finder crosses Agent Host to SDK catalog.search
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per enabled effective source for the initial page, with bounded continuation pages; adding plugin to the SDK kinds array does not add another call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Search already used the same source fan-out and SDK request count; the diff broadens the candidate kinds in that request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All selected source requests for a page are joined before merged results return.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled source count, query result page size, and at most the existing bounded filtered backfill page count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One concurrent request per selected source; continuation pages are sequential per user scroll/backfill.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Marketplace continuations retain buffered items in an LRU with expiry; Agent Host candidate handles are retained for four minutes with a 1,000-entry cap. Empty/error behavior remains bounded by source state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the nonempty-query branch excludes saved feeds and preserves one bounded SDK search.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin candidates may change payload composition, but page and retention caps remain unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: plugin support expands a bounded existing request without increasing boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install a curated skill, MCP server, or plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user-triggered flow prepares an exact plan, waits for confirmation, applies it, and for plugins waits for the local plugin inventory observable before firing the change event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare and apply SDK installation plans through Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one prepare/plan and one apply per user-confirmed installation. If a retained selection expired, prepare performs one exact SDK catalog search before planning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Skills/MCP already used confirmed plan/apply; direct catalog plugins were rejected. The diff enables the equivalent bounded plugin flow and returns verified identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both plan and apply are sequential on the explicit install critical path; plugin completion additionally waits for local inventory, bounded by 30 seconds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected customization; plugin review metadata scales with the SDK plan's file list only to compute a count/byte total, not to render every file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No burst: prepare, confirmation, apply, and inventory synchronization are sequential for one user action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh retained candidates avoid repeat catalog search; expired handles trigger one exact search. Pending operations are deleted after apply/failure, and catalog associations are bounded in memory.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: plan/apply and inventory synchronization paths are explicit and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK plan/apply duration depends on plugin size and network, but invocation count is fixed and user initiated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new work is necessary for the requested plugin installation and does not fan out with collection size.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restart/reload and reconcile installed plugin identity
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider inventory is read, projected into installation records, and exact repository/path/version matching determines installed state; no catalog retrieval is required for authoritative inventory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory request per refresh/session, plus an in-process read of the plugin observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider already listed receipts and plugin inventory; the diff changes association and identity projection, not list-call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Inventory completion gates refreshed installed state, as before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed receipt/plugin count and the visible catalog candidate count used by existing matching logic.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single provider inventory refresh; matching is local and synchronous over bounded current snapshots.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Receipt snapshots are cached by a bounded number of backend sessions; catalog presentation associations are bounded and installation identity remains authoritative without a warm catalog.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: no new restart-time remote boundary or unbounded state was introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed collection sizes vary, but the added normalization/comparison is constant work per existing match and adds no boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: synchronization preserves existing boundary cardinality and bounded cache ownership.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 27 changed files. Submitted one medium boundary-fanout finding for the redundant full catalog query on successful curated Browse loads; plugin search/install, inventory synchronization, icon handling, cache lifecycle, cleanup, and concurrency were otherwise bounded or preserved existing cardinality.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
